title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer to parity with OpenAI semantics for params, roles, stop/logprobs, and response formatting, while improving streaming stability and function/tool call handling. This change unifies parameter parsing, makes role handling deterministic, restores logprobs/stop behavior parity, and tightens streaming backpressure and retry behavior for client-facing endpoints.

Summary of changes: consolidated param handling to accept both OpenAI and Redwood idioms; canonicalized role normalization (user/system/assistant) and stricter validation; implemented stop-token handling that respects multiple stop sequences and backwards-compatible logprobs behavior when requested; reworked streaming pump to ensure single-writer semantics and reduced jitter on partial chunks; improved function/tool call payload shaping and added structured output hints for tools; doc updates describing compatibility guarantees and sample payloads.

Compatibility: Backwards-compatible for most customers. A small set of clients that relied on previous permissive role names (e.g. "assistant_bot") will now receive a validation error; migration guidance included in docs. Default behavior remains unchanged unless opt-in params are used (e.g. include_logprobs).

Testing: extensive unit tests added and integration tests against the OpenAI conformance harness. Ran long-running streaming stability job for 48 hours in perf-canary. Benchmarked memory usage and latency impact; median latency unchanged, p95 improved by ~6% under burst load due to batching adjustments.

Rollout plan: staged rollout via feature flag per region: canary (us-west) -> gradual (us-west/eu) -> global. Rollback path implemented, and fallback to legacy compat layer when downstream reporters detect regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Param parsing and aliases implemented
- [x] Role normalization and validation
- [x] stop tokens and logprobs parity behavior
- [x] Streaming stability fixes and retries
- [x] Structured output and function/tool calling shaping
- [x] Docs and migration guide updated

Related: closes ENG-1342, addresses SUP-421.

review_comments: Diego Martín: Left nits in chat_completions.rs - prefer early returns for validation to keep stack traces small.
Priya Rao: Can we add a small e2e that exercises multiple stop sequences with streaming enabled? I saw one edge case where partial streaming chunk cut the stop token boundary.
Liam O'Connor: Streaming retry behavior LGTM, but please document potential duplicate token emission on exact-boundary retry and the mitigation in SDKs.
Author (Ava Chen): Responded - added early returns, added e2e test case for multi-stop under streaming, and documented duplicate-token mitigation in docs and Python SDK.
